records.title: PV Insights
records.comments:
After a year of follow-up with the Medical and Commercial teams, the LMS team successfully re-engaged externally by delivering Safety Concerns Training at Al Amal Hospital, the largest psychiatric hospital in the UAE. This marks the second training conducted for Spravato since its launch across all Gulf countries.
The training was initiated following a request from the Sales Manager to address the growing need for education, as many new nurses have joined the hospital and existing staff required a refresher on Risk Minimization Measures (RMMs) and safety concerns management.
The presentation emphasized:

The responsibility of healthcare professionals (HCPs) in Adverse Event (AE) reporting.
Awareness of Spravato’s safety concerns.
The additional RMMs implemented by the company to ensure patient safety.

Audience: Over 20 nurses, including the Head of the Nursing Department.
records.feedback: This engagement reinforced LMS’s role as a key representative of the medication’s safety profile during external interactions with HCPs. The feedback from the meeting was highly positive, strengthening LMS’s position within the team. Based on this success, LMS has been invited to conduct another training in Oman.

records.title: PV Insights
records.comments:
Based on the Sales Manager’s request, a Safety Concerns Training session was delivered at Al Masarra Hospital, the largest psychiatric hospital in Oman. This marks the first training conducted for Spravato since its launch in Oman.
The training was initiated to address the growing need for education, as many new nurses have joined the hospital and existing staff required a refresher on Risk Minimization Measures (RMMs) and safety concerns management.
Key Focus Areas

The responsibility of healthcare professionals (HCPs) in Adverse Event (AE) reporting.
Awareness of Spravato’s safety concerns.
The additional RMMs implemented by the company to ensure patient safety.

Audience
The session was attended by over 40 healthcare professionals, including physicians, pharmacists, and nurses. The training emphasized our shared responsibility as a pharmaceutical company and HCPs to ensure patient safety, awareness of the medication’s safety profile, and the importance and value of reporting safety events.
Post-Training Engagement
Following the training, we engaged with the Head of Clinical Pharmacy, Head of Nursing, and Physicians, discussing:

Ways to increase awareness of safety reporting.
Gathering feedback on patient needs.
Exploring additional measures to enhance value.
records.feedback:
The feedback from the training at Al Masarra Hospital was highly positive. Attendees appreciated the active involvement of the company’s safety team in raising awareness about our shared responsibility for safety reporting to ensure patient safety.
Following this session, the Sales Manager informed us that the local Health Authority (HA) in Oman has raised several questions regarding:

What is Spravato?
Why does it have multiple educational materials?
Why is training required for nurses and HCPs?
Why must patients receive the medication in a hospital setting under HCP supervision?

To address these concerns, the Sales Manager requested that we prepare and deliver a specific presentation covering:

Spravato’s safety profile, summarizing key safety concerns.
How the company designed additional Risk Minimization Measures (aRMMs) to manage these concerns.
The LMS structure and the engagement activities conducted by the safety team with external HCPs to increase awareness and ensure patient safety as part of J&J’s commitment.

records.title: PV Insights
records.comments:
Throughout 2025, LMS has been actively exploring Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (PAH) patient needs and identifying gaps in the patient journey that impact patient safety. The most significant concern identified was medication adherence for PAH treatments (Opsumit & Uptravi), primarily due to challenges in managing adverse events such as headache and gastrointestinal (GIT) side effects.
Proposed Solution
During the cycle meeting, LMS presented a comprehensive plan to:

Create a patient support group that brings together well-controlled, stable patients with uncontrolled patients.
Facilitate experience sharing on:

How to adhere to prescribed medications.
How to manage adverse events effectively.



Rationale
For years, communication and training efforts have focused on HCPs (physicians and nurses). Despite this, many patients continue to face challenges with disease management and medication adherence. HCPs and nurses often struggle to convey practical strategies for managing the disease and its associated adverse events.
Purpose of the initiative:

Directly engage patients through:

Patient Support Program Nurse
Trained Patient Ambassador
Patient Engagement Manager
records.feedback:
The Sales, Marketing, and Medical teams fully supported the proposal, recognizing its potential to:

Improve adherence and compliance.
Encourage HCPs to initiate Uptravi for eligible patients who may be hesitant due to AE concerns.
Support dose optimization for patients requiring effective therapeutic levels.
Deliver a positive impact on patient safety and, if successful, drive improved outcomes and business performance.
Create significant strategic value at this time, especially with the launch of Opsynvi in the UAE, by reinforcing J&J’s commitment to patient-centric care and safety.
